methodologyNotes: Roster covers twelve ballistic chronographs spanning Doppler-radar units (Garmin, LabRadar, Athlon, Caldwell VelociRadar), optical light-gate units (Competition Electronics, Shooting Chrony, base Caldwell Ballistic Precision line), and muzzle-mounted magnetic/strain-gauge units (MagnetoSpeed), verified 2026-08-11 against manufacturer product pages (garmin.com, mylabradar.com, caldwellshooting.com, competitionelectronics.com, magnetospeed.com, athlonoptics.com, shootingchrony.com) and corroborated by major retailers and outdoor-press reviews (American Rifleman, Outdoor Life, Pew Pew Tactical, MidwayUSA, OpticsPlanet). Fields left null (velocity_range_fps, accuracy_pct, shot_capacity, operating_temp_range, weight_oz on several entries) reflect specs genuinely not published by the manufacturer or not independently confirmable from the sources actually fetched, rather than an inferred/estimated value. Two adversarial corrections were made to the seed list: (1) "Competition Electronics ProChrono LTR" does not exist in Competition Electronics' current or historical lineup (DLX, LTD, Digital, Pal); the seed was replaced with the actual non-Bluetooth economy sibling of the DLX, the ProChrono LTD, which American Rifleman and OpticsPlanet confirm shares the DLX's velocity range, accuracy, and memory capacity but omits Bluetooth. (2) "Athlon Rangecraft" is a shorthand for Athlon Optics' actual current product, the "Rangecraft Velocity PRO Radar Chronograph" — full model name used. The seed's generic "Ballistic Precision Chronograph" and "Caldwell Ballistic Precision G2" are two distinct, still-current Caldwell products (base optical unit at caldwellshooting.com/.../720001.html vs. the higher-accuracy G2 at .../720002.html) and are both retained as separate entries rather than treated as duplicates. accessedAt 2026-08-11 throughout.

products.name: Garmin Xero C1 Pro Chronograph
products.priceNote: Garmin.com MSRP; some retailers list a bundle/base configuration nearer $499.99

specs.velocity_range_fps: 100-5,000 (firearms); air rifle to 2,000; airsoft to 1,000; arrows to 600
specs.shot_capacity: continuous logging to onboard memory plus ShotView app; no fixed string/shot limit published
specs.battery_type_runtime: internal rechargeable Li-ion, USB-C charge; rated for ~2,000 shots or 6 hours continuous use per charge

products.provenance: Garmin's own product page (garmin.com/en-US/p/771164/) and Garmin Support pages confirm the 100-5,000 fps range for firearms (2,000 fps air rifle / 1,000 fps airsoft / 600 fps arrows), IPX7 rating, ShotView app pairing, and that the unit is not muzzle-blast triggered (works with suppressors/muzzle brakes). Accuracy (±0.1%), battery runtime (2,000 shots / 6 hrs), and physical dimensions/weight (2.38 x 3 x 1.35 in., 3.5 oz) corroborated by Outdoor Life and Pew Pew Tactical field reviews. Operating temperature range was not stated on any fetched source, so left null rather than assumed.

products.name: LabRadar Ballistic Velocity Doppler Radar Chronograph (V1)
products.priceNote: Original LabRadar MSRP; now frequently discounted ($449.99 at MidSouth Shooters) as it sits below the newer LX in LabRadar's own lineup

specs.shot_capacity: records to microSD card; can extrapolate velocity at up to 5 downrange distances to 100 yd
specs.bluetooth_app: Wi-Fi hotspot to companion app (no Bluetooth)
specs.battery_type_runtime: 6x AA batteries, or USB power bank / wall adapter

products.provenance: LabRadar's current site (mylabradar.com) still lists the original unit alongside the LX. Velocity range (65-3,900 fps), ±0.1% accuracy, 6x AA / USB power options, and 5-distance extrapolation confirmed via American Rifleman's original review; operating temperature (-10 to 40 C) and total packaged weight (5 lb 11.2 oz = 91.2 oz, unit plus stand and external power supply) sourced from the same review, so weight_oz reflects the packaged figure rather than bare-unit weight, which was not separately published. The device connects to its companion app via a self-hosted Wi-Fi network, not Bluetooth.

products.name: LabRadar LX Doppler Radar Chronograph
products.priceNote: LabRadar MSRP, consistent across Scheels, MidwayUSA, and Powder Valley Outdoors

specs.shot_capacity: integrated onboard memory, session-based logging; exact string/shot cap not published

products.provenance: LabRadar's official LX product page confirms 60GHz Doppler operation, integrated rechargeable battery, LCD display, and Bluetooth connectivity with a built-in IPSC/USPSA/IDPA power-factor calculator. Velocity range (65-5,003 fps) and physical dimensions/weight (2.5 x 2.75 x 2.75 in., 11.5 oz without tripod) corroborated by American Rifleman's and NRA Shooting Sports Journal's LX coverage. A specific published accuracy percentage and operating temperature range for the LX (distinct from the original unit's spec sheet) were not found on any fetched source, so both are left null rather than carried over by assumption from the V1 model.

products.name: Caldwell Ballistic Precision G2 Chronograph
products.priceNote: Caldwell MSRP; street price commonly seen $239.99-$379.99 depending on retailer/kit

specs.sensing_method: optical (inverted light-sensor gates, 18 in. spacing, self-contained LED sunscreens)

products.provenance: Caldwell's own G2 product page (SKU 720002) and retailer copy (GunMag Warehouse, Firearms Depot, Amazon) confirm the inverted light-sensor design with 18 in. gate spacing and self-contained LED sunscreens for low-light accuracy, a 48 MHz processor with factory computer calibration, ±0.25% accuracy across a 5-9,999 fps range, Bluetooth connectivity, and a rechargeable Li-ion battery with FPS/MPS display toggle. Shot-string memory capacity, precise unit weight, and operating temperature range were not stated on any fetched source and are left null rather than estimated.

products.name: Competition Electronics ProChrono DLX Chronograph
products.priceNote: Competition Electronics does not display consumer pricing on its own site (competitionelectronics.com); retailers (Walmart, Lancaster Archery, Pyramyd Air) commonly list $140-$170

specs.shot_capacity: up to 9 shot strings of up to 99 shots each
specs.battery_type_runtime: one 9V alkaline battery, rated ~20+ hours runtime

products.provenance: Competition Electronics' own product page confirms the 20-9,999 fps range, ±0.5% or better accuracy, 16 x 4 x 3.25 in. / 2.1 lb (33.6 oz) housing, 9-string x 99-shot memory, 20-100 F rated operating range, single 9V battery power, and onboard Bluetooth for iOS/Android — differentiating this DLX model from the non-Bluetooth ProChrono LTD below. No fixed consumer price is published by the manufacturer, so priceUsd is left null with the observed retail range noted.

products.name: Competition Electronics ProChrono LTD Chronograph
products.priceNote: Competition Electronics own product page (competitionelectronics.com/products/prochrono-ltd, SKU CEI-3825) lists $119.95; this non-Bluetooth economy tier sits below the DLX

specs.shot_capacity: up to 9 shot strings of up to 99 shots each
specs.battery_type_runtime: one 9V alkaline battery, rated ~20 hours runtime

products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: "Competition Electronics ProChrono LTR" is not a real product — Competition Electronics' current and historical lineup consists of the ProChrono DLX, ProChrono LTD, ProChrono Digital, and ProChrono Pal (confirmed directly on competitionelectronics.com/products/*). The seed was replaced with the ProChrono LTD, which American Rifleman's preview and OpticsPlanet's listing confirm as the DLX's non-Bluetooth economy sibling, sharing an identical 20-9,999 fps range, ±0.5% accuracy, 9-string x 99-shot memory, and physical dimensions/weight with the DLX, differing only in the omission of Bluetooth connectivity and a full built-in user interface in its place.

products.name: Shooting Chrony Beta Master Chronograph
products.priceNote: Street price varies widely by retailer and condition, roughly $99.99-$198.19

specs.shot_capacity: 60-shot memory across 6 individual strings (2-10 shots each)
specs.battery_type_runtime: one 9V alkaline battery, rated ~48 hours continuous use

products.provenance: Shooting Chrony's own model-comparison page (shootingchrony.com) and retailer spec sheets (Top Gun Supply, OpticsPlanet, Airfield Shooting Club review) confirm the 30-7,000 fps range, better-than-0.5% accuracy, 20-gauge steel housing under 2 lb 8 oz (used here as 39 oz), 16 ft remote control cord, single 9V alkaline battery good for ~48 hours, and 60-shot memory across 6 strings of 2-10 shots. No Bluetooth or app connectivity exists on this model (wired remote display only); operating temperature range was not published on any fetched source and is left null.

products.name: Athlon Optics Rangecraft Velocity PRO Radar Chronograph
products.priceNote: Athlon Optics own product page (athlonoptics.com, SKU 707301) lists $499.99
products.provenance: CORRECTED FROM SEED: "Athlon Rangecraft" is shorthand for Athlon Optics' actual current product, the Rangecraft Velocity PRO Radar Chronograph (full name used here). Athlon's own product page and corroborating retailer listings (Cabela's, Scheels, MidwayUSA) confirm Doppler-radar sensing (no barrel mount needed), a 65-5,000 fps range, 2.4 in. LCD display, IP67 rating, 14-122 F operating range, 50-session x 100-shot memory, internal rechargeable Li-ion battery, Athlon Ballistics App pairing, and a combined chronograph+tripod weight of 9 oz. A specific stated accuracy percentage was not found on any fetched source and is left null rather than assumed from competing radar units.

products.name: MagnetoSpeed V3 Ballistic Chronograph
products.priceNote: magnetospeed.com current listing for the V3 kit; hard-case and bundle configurations across retailers range roughly $180-$450

specs.shot_capacity: continuous rapid-mode data logging with rate-of-fire and bracket tracking; not string-limited like optical units
specs.battery_type_runtime: one 9V battery, or two CR123 batteries

products.provenance: MagnetoSpeed's own site confirms the V3 mounts like a bayonet on barrels/suppressors from 1/2 in. up to 2 in. diameter (with 1 in. extra blast-zone clearance for muzzle devices up to ~3 in.), features a 3-button menu, advanced data logging, rapid mode with rate-of-fire and bracket tracking, dual data connection points, and runs on a single 9V or two CR123 batteries. Accuracy is stated by the manufacturer only as a 99.5%-99.9% figure rather than a fps range or explicit ± percent, reproduced here as a derived ±0.1-0.5% range; a specific fps measurement range, precise unit weight, and operating temperature were not found on any fetched source and are left null. The V3 has no Bluetooth/app connectivity (standalone LCD display only).

products.name: MagnetoSpeed Sporter Ballistics Chronograph
products.priceNote: magnetospeed.com listing price; frequently discounted by retailers (seen as low as $74.99)
products.provenance: MagnetoSpeed's own site and TFB/Long Range Only reviews confirm the Sporter is a stripped-down two-piece design (muzzle-mounted bayonet sensor plus a single-9V, single-button display unit), intended for center-fire rifles and revolvers only (not air guns or rimfire), fitting barrels 1/2 in. to 1 in. diameter with muzzle devices up to 2.7 in. long. A specific fps measurement range, accuracy percentage, shot-memory capacity, unit weight, and operating temperature were not stated on any fetched source and are left null rather than carried over by assumption from the V3 model, whose electronics differ. No Bluetooth/app connectivity exists on this model.

products.name: Caldwell VelociRadar Chronograph
products.priceNote: Walmart current retail; other retailers range from $304.96 (Firearms Depot) to $549.99 (Blackland Arms)
products.provenance: Caldwell's own VelociRadar product page (SKU 1134904) confirms 60Hz active Chirp radar tracking bullet velocity and distance up to 100 yd downrange, ±0.1% true-muzzle-velocity accuracy, a 2.8 in. color screen, 100-session x 100-shot memory, Bluetooth pairing with the Caldwell smartphone app, a built-in rechargeable Li-ion battery, and an included recoil-activated trigger and ball-head tripod. A specific fps measurement range and unit weight were not stated on the fetched source and are left null rather than assumed from the similarly-radar-based VelociRadar's competitors.

products.name: Caldwell Ballistic Precision Chronograph
products.priceNote: Base non-Bluetooth model; Caldwell's own site separately lists a Bluetooth variant at $168.99 and Premium Kit bundles at $214.99-$236.99
products.provenance: Retained as a distinct entry from the Caldwell Ballistic Precision G2 (SKU 720002): Caldwell's site lists this base unit separately at SKU 720001, alongside separate Bluetooth ($168.99) and Premium Kit ($214.99-$236.99) SKUs, indicating a genuinely different, lower-tier product line rather than a duplicate of the G2. Guns.com's gear review and Caldwell's own product family page confirm the shared underlying architecture (48 MHz processor, factory-calibrated inverted light-sensor gates, ±0.25% accuracy, 5-9,999 fps range, FPS/MPS toggle) across the Ballistic Precision family, but the base 720001 model's own battery type, shot-memory capacity, and operating temperature were not separately confirmed from the G2's on any fetched source, so those fields are left null rather than copied across from the G2 entry.
